title: Simplify the authentication boundary and controller contract
objective: Define the shared Authorize(ctx) and auth.Scope(allowed...) contract, then validate one fail-closed authentication decision in an Endpoint gRPC pilot before any broader API migration.
verified_current_state: User, project, organization, and service credentials are authenticated by separate middleware.
Multiple middleware can inspect the same request and write different authentication values into the shared CTX_ context slot.
Several credential middleware silently continue when credentials are missing or rejected.
Controllers repeat GetSimplePrincipleGRPC or GetAuthPrinciple plus RequireUser and RequireProject checks.
ResolveAuditActor currently has no production caller.
Organization credential authentication exists, but organization credentials do not yet expose a durable credential actor ID.
acceptance_criteria: Every protected Endpoint gRPC unary and stream request reaches exactly one authentication decision in the pilot.
Protected requests with no credential, malformed credentials, rejected credentials, or multiple credential classes fail before the controller runs.
Exactly one AuthenticationPrinciple is written to the existing CTX_ request context key after successful authentication.
Controllers obtain authentication only through types.Authorize(ctx).
Authorize reads the existing CTX_ context key directly and does not call an authenticationFromContext-style helper.
Controllers declare allowed authentication types only through auth.Scope(allowed...).
Scope returns the authenticated principle when its concrete authentication type is allowed and returns an error otherwise.
No new authentication-time project or organization mutation is introduced; the Endpoint pilot documents and tests the temporary existing user x-project-id SwitchProject compatibility behavior.
Resource authorization remains explicit and separate from authentication-type validation.
Intentionally public routes remain accessible through explicit public registration or policy.
No raw credential, token, or secret appears in logs, errors, context keys, or audit identity.
Legacy authentication middleware and accessors are removed only after every caller migrates.

scope_semantics.allowed_match: Return the same authenticated principle when its concrete AuthType appears in the allowed list.
scope_semantics.resource_authorization: Scope validates caller class only and never grants organization, project, assistant, endpoint, or other resource access.

contract.authorize: Read the existing CTX_ key directly, require a non-nil authenticated AuthenticationPrinciple, and return ErrUnauthenticated otherwise.
contract.scope: Validate the concrete authentication type against explicitly allowed AuthType values and return the same authenticated principle or an error.
prohibited_abstractions: generic context getter or setter utilities
registry or plugin frameworks for four known credential types
new wrapper types without a demonstrated controller or service requirement

implementation_sequence.name: contract
changes: Define Authorize(ctx) and the Scope contract in pkg/types while reusing the existing CTX_ key.
Implement Scope directly on concrete authentication principles rather than introducing utility layers.
Retain UserIdentityProvider, OrganizationContextProvider, ProjectContextProvider, DelegatedContextProvider, and current resource-authorization behavior during the pilot.

implementation_sequence.name: coordinating middleware
changes: Create coordinating gRPC unary and stream authentication middleware for the Endpoint pilot.
Extract credential presence once and reject missing, malformed, or conflicting protected requests.
Dispatch to the existing user, project, organization, or service authenticator.
Write exactly one successful authentication value directly with context.WithValue.

implementation_sequence.name: endpoint pilot
changes: Replace the Endpoint API credential middleware chain with the coordinating middleware.
Migrate every Endpoint gRPC controller from GetSimplePrincipleGRPC entry checks to Authorize(ctx) and Scope in the same binary-level slice.
Keep Endpoint Gin /readiness/ and /healthz/ public and outside the gRPC authentication boundary.
Treat every method registered by EndpointService and Deployment as protected.
Validate user, project, organization, and service credential authentication before considering broad migration.

implementation_sequence.name: pilot decision gate
changes: Review the complete Endpoint middleware and controller migration before expanding scope.
Inventory public routes and credential sources independently for Assistant, Integration, and Web.
Create separately approved follow-up plans for each remaining binary.
Defer legacy middleware deletion until every binary has migrated and rollback windows have closed.

rules: Any presented user tuple field selects the user credential class.
authorization and x-auth-id are both required.
x-auth-id and optional x-project-id must be non-zero unsigned integers.
Existing user x-project-id and SwitchProject behavior remains as an explicit temporary pilot exception because Endpoint services still require selected project context.
The pilot cannot expand to another binary until an approved resource-authorization design removes authentication-time SwitchProject.
Remove only one leading rpd-prj- prefix.
A presented but rejected organization credential fails closed instead of continuing unauthenticated.
A presented but rejected service credential fails closed.

credential_compatibility.conflicts: Reject every request presenting more than one of user, project, organization, or service credential classes.
credential_compatibility.failure_response: Return gRPC Unauthenticated with the stable public message invalid authentication credentials; log only credential class and failure category.

out_of_scope_behavior: Audit persistence schema or dual-write migration.
Organization credential persistence or credential management APIs.

principles.kiss: Expose only Authorize(ctx) and auth.Scope(allowed...) to controllers and keep four concrete credential paths explicit.
principles.yagni: Do not create context utilities, scope utilities, registries, plugins, wrappers, or generalized policy engines.
principles.single_ownership: The coordinating middleware owns credential selection and the single context write; concrete authenticators own credential verification; controllers own allowed authentication types.
principles.single_source_of_truth: The existing CTX_ request context key contains exactly one AuthenticationPrinciple; new Endpoint controllers use Authorize(ctx) while unchanged packages may continue reading that same value during staged rollout.
principles.explicit_contracts: Missing credentials, conflicting classes, rejected credentials, allowed authentication types, public routes, and resource authorization boundaries are visible in code.
principles.fail_safe: Every protected authentication failure returns before controller execution.
principles.observability: Log only authentication class and failure category, never credential material.
principles.least_privilege: Scope validates only explicitly listed authentication types and does not grant resource access by itself.
principles.reversibility: Pilot only Endpoint and retain its previous middleware and accessors until the pilot review permits cleanup.
principles.open_source_readability: Prefer direct Go code and named interfaces over hidden helpers, reflection, metaprogramming, or framework-style abstractions.

required_tests: Authorize rejects missing, nil, and unauthenticated context values.
Authorize returns each valid concrete user, project, organization, and service principle.
Scope accepts every explicitly allowed authentication type and rejects every omitted type.
Endpoint unary and stream middleware reject missing credentials on protected methods.
Endpoint unary and stream middleware reject malformed, rejected, and conflicting credentials before controller execution.
Endpoint unary and stream middleware authenticate each user, project, organization, and service credential path.
Exactly one authentication value is visible to the controller.
Endpoint /readiness/ and /healthz/ remain accessible without credentials.
Endpoint controller tests cover allowed multi-scope access and rejected unlisted authentication types across the migrated controller package.
Resource authorization tests remain separate from authentication-type tests.
Credential tests preserve user tuple rules, project prefix handling, organization and service failure behavior, every cross-class conflict, and the stable gRPC error mapping.
Authorize and legacy accessors read the same single CTX_ value during staged rollout; tests prove there is no dual context write.
Logs and errors contain no raw credential values.
risks: Global gRPC interceptors can accidentally protect future public methods unless the Endpoint public inventory remains reviewed and tested.
Changing missing-credential behavior from pass-through to rejection can expose callers that relied on accidental anonymous access.
Migrating authentication and resource authorization together can create an oversized change; keep them as separate checks.
Concrete principles may not currently expose all resource context required by services; do not solve that by adding fake identity methods.
Organization authentication can succeed without project context; project-specific access requires a separately approved project-selection and resource-authorization rule.
Temporary user SwitchProject compatibility contradicts the target separation and must block expansion beyond Endpoint until resolved.
Deleting legacy accessors during the pilot would prevent binary-level rollback and is prohibited.
rollback: Revert Endpoint transport wiring and the Endpoint controller package to the previous credential middleware and context accessor behavior. The pilot reuses CTX_ and retains existing authenticators, capability providers, legacy middleware, and accessors, so rollback requires no schema, protobuf, SDK, or credential changes.

discussion.decision: APPROVE documentation-only draft; implementation remains blocked
open_blockers: Define how an organization-authenticated caller selects and proves access to a project-specific Endpoint operation without mutating authentication identity.
Define the resource-authorization replacement for user x-project-id SwitchProject before expanding the authentication boundary beyond Endpoint.
